chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem with the fasting one swallowing his own mucus.

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Does swallowing one's own mucus break the fast according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify a common practical doubt during fasting, establishing that swallowing one's own naturally produced mucus does not break the fast. This ruling distinguishes between internal bodily fluids, which are considered part of the body, and external substances, thereby providing ease (*taysir*) for the fasting individual in their daily worship. The hadith reflects the Shia juristic principle of presuming the validity of the fast unless there is clear evidence of invalidation by a foreign entity.
